Saint-Gilles — Brussels, Belgium

In detail

Saint-Gilles is one of the 19 official communes of the Brussels-Capital Region. BISA (Brussels Institute for Statistics and Analysis), citing Federale Politie figures, recorded 11,114 total registered crimes and misdemeanours here in 2025, across a population of 48,827 residents (Statbel, 2025) — a rate of 22,762 offences per 100,000 residents, roughly 1.9x the citywide commune average. This rate is calculated against registered residents, not footfall, so a busy central, station, or nightlife-heavy commune can read higher without that meaning it is unusually risky to walk through, and a quiet residential commune can show a low rate simply by having few offences relative to its population. Saint-Gilles is home to Gare du Midi — Brussels' Eurostar and international rail hub, and one of Europe's busiest stations — plus the Barrière/Parvis nightlife area, both of which draw far more people through the commune than its resident count alone would suggest, which pushes its per-resident rate up without that meaning elevated risk per visit. This is Wandroz's official-data layer for Brussels — real BISA / Federale Politie and Statbel figures, not a qualitative or press-based judgment — and the source data is not split here by time of day, so both figures shown here are the same.

Frequently asked questions

Is Saint-Gilles safe?

Wandroz currently rates Saint-Gilles in Brussels as an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Brussels. This rating is derived from BISA / Federale Politie's official crime statistics — an official statistic, not an assessment. High-footfall tourist, transit or shopping areas can read higher on this kind of measure without that meaning elevated risk per visit, since these statistics are normalised against registered residents rather than footfall — see the note on this page and the methodology page for the full caveats. The source data has no day/night breakdown, so this single rating applies at any time of day rather than being a distinct night-specific figure.

Does Saint-Gilles's rating differ between day and night?

No — Saint-Gilles's source data has no time-of-day breakdown, so the same rating (an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Brussels) is shown for both day and night rather than Wandroz inventing a separate night figure it doesn't actually have.

Is Saint-Gilles a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Saint-Gilles's day rating (an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Brussels) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late. The Booking.com link on this page searches Saint-Gilles itself.
